# Nexus Guard

> Connect your agents once. Link your services once.

Nexus Guard is a project-aware scaffold for coding-agent service access, built with
Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, and Rust. Status: scaffold, not yet MVP. Linux first.
MVP scope: Supabase-only (+ GitHub native adapter spike, labeled). Agents reach
one persistent local Nexus over HTTP-only (`http://localhost:<port>/mcp`).

## Canonical chain

Agent → Session → Project → Environment → Service → Account → Resource → Capability → Policy Decision

- Supabase + Koupa ≠ Supabase + Nabdh
- Supabase + production ≠ Supabase + development

## MVP scope

- Local desktop app + local runtime (Linux first)
- Project registry + `.nexus/project.json` (authoritative, secret-free config)
- One provider: Supabase (+ GitHub spike, labeled)
- Single HTTP transport only (`http://localhost:<port>/mcp`)
- Multiple concurrent agent sessions, isolated by project
- Minimal Guard: allow / warn / require approval / block (full policy engine deferred-paid)
- Local audit log (secret-free)
- Agent-facing MCP interface: `nexus.context`, `nexus.request_access`, `nexus.execute`

## What Nexus is not

- Not a generic secrets vault or password manager
- Not an enterprise governance/compliance platform
- Not a filesystem sandbox; its boundary is infrastructure access
- Not a full policy engine in MVP (minimal Guard only)
- An action outside Nexus is unmanaged, not protected

## Key rules

- Only the developer can change policy; agents cannot grant access or disable Guard.
- Missing or conflicting project identity stops the request; Nexus never silently guesses.
- Secrets stay in OS secure storage; repos hold only safe references.
- Warn ≠ block; approval is explicit.

- Website: https://nexus-guard.nafaa-store.workers.dev

- Prototype evidence: `cargo test --manifest-path prototype/nexus-check/Cargo.toml`
